name: industry_group_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Within tightly correlated industry sub-groups (e.g., private banks, PSU banks, IT services, generic pharma), individual stock returns tend to revert to the group mean within the same trading day. When a stock deviates >15 bps from its industry group average return, the deviation is likely noise (order flow imbalance, temporary liquidity events) rather than stock-specific news. The inefficiency persists because: (1) most traders analyze stocks individually, not relative to their industry group, (2) constructing real-time industry group baskets requires infrastructure, (3) the reversion window is 10-30 minutes — too slow for HFTs, too fast for fundamentals-driven traders. In Indian markets, industry groups have historically high within-group correlations (0.6-0.8 for private banks, 0.5-0.7 for IT services) making this signal reliable.
universe: 6 industry groups: private banks (5), PSU banks (5), IT services (4), generic pharma (4), cement (4), auto OEMs (4)
stock_filter: Top 4-5 stocks by market cap in each industry group, ADV > ₹20 crore

other: industry group constituent list and weights (equal-weighted)

indicators.name: group_avg_return
indicators.formula: mean(cum_return_bps) across all stocks in industry group from 09:15

indicators.name: group_correlation
indicators.formula: average pairwise rolling_corr(stock_i, stock_j, 60) within group

conditions: stock has no specific news today
long.confirmation: deviation_zscore starts rising (crosses above -1.7 from below -2.0)

conditions: stock has no specific news today
short.confirmation: deviation_zscore starts falling (crosses below 1.7 from above 2.0)

entry.entry_price: limit order at midprice on confirmation bar

exit.target: stock_deviation reverts to 0 (stock returns to group average)
exit.stop_loss: deviation_zscore extends to ±3.0 (deviation widening — likely news-driven)
exit.trailing_stop: none (target is full reversion to group mean)
exit.signal_exit: group_correlation drops below 0.3 (group dispersion, reversion fails)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L on divergent stock (directional on the stock, hedged by group mean expectation)

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (intra-group reversion works across vol regimes)
filters.time_filter: skip first 15 min (group relationships establishing) and last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: divergent stock volume > 50th percentile of its typical volume
filters.trend_filter: no trend filter (relative reversion is trend-independent)
filters.event_filter: skip stocks with scheduled results, AGMs, or corporate actions today
other_filters: skip if divergent stock is the only one moving (all others flat — it's the divergent stock that has news)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — within-group mean reversion is driven by structural correlation in fundamentals. As long as companies in the same industry share common drivers (rates for banks, INR for IT), the signal persists.

weaknesses: Stock-specific news (analyst upgrade/downgrade, management commentary, deal wins) can cause legitimate divergence that doesn't revert. The 'no news' filter is imperfect.
Within-group correlation is not constant — on result season days, correlations drop as individual earnings drive stocks, reducing signal reliability.
Equal-weighted group averages may not be appropriate when one stock dominates the group by market cap (e.g., HDFC Bank in private banks).
prior_art: Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) 'Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule' — the foundational statistical arbitrage paper. Avellaneda & Lee (2010) 'Statistical Arbitrage in the US Equities Market'. In India, Bhushan & Singh (2014) test pairs trading in NSE.
notes: Maintain a daily updated list of industry group constituents. Stocks may be added or removed from groups based on business changes (e.g., HDFC merged with HDFC Bank, changing the private bank group). Use a 20-day rolling correlation to validate group membership before each session.
